title: Choose sensitivity for the game's movement demands
summary: Sensitivity should be chosen around the movement and aiming demands of the game or role. Faster, wider-angle games often reward faster settings than angle-holding tac shooters.
why: Apex-style wide-angle, faster-movement aiming usually pushes toward faster sensitivities than Valorant-style angle holding.
Even inside one game, different roles or situations can reward different balances of stability, quick angle clearing, arm range, and wrist speed.
actions: Pick a main match sensitivity that fits the game's most common movement and angle demands.
When swapping games or roles, expect the optimal sensitivity balance to shift with them instead of forcing one universal number.
If a slower setting helps hold angles but makes quick clears too heavy, adjust until both tasks are reasonably covered.
avoid: Do not keep one slow tactical sens in every game out of habit alone.
Avoid copying another game's sensitivity logic without checking the movement style first.

evidence.claim: Different games and roles can justify different sensitivities because the movement patterns and aiming demands are not the same.
evidence.excerpt: Apex tends to reward faster settings than Valorant, and even roles inside games can push the optimal balance in different directions.
